claims.statement: Ask is a single deep agent built by build_agent() with a fixed TOOLS list of seven tools (db_list_tables, db_describe_table, db_profile_column, db_query, search_graph, fetch_url, compare_fit) plus read_file and ls for skill reading; it has no subagents and no task tool, and tests pin the exact tool set.

harness.install() registers a HarnessProfile disabling deepagents' general-purpose subagent for all supported providers, and harness.filesystem() replaces the default FilesystemMiddleware per agent so only the kept tools (read_file, ls for Ask) are registered; nothing that writes is exposed.

Every Ask tool wraps its body in try/except and returns an error string instead of raising, because a raised tool exception would abort the whole run; the db_query rejection and failure prefixes are a wire format that the retry limiter matches.

Ask has four on-demand skills (funder-matching, funder-comparison, funder-shortlist-brief, news-brief) loaded by the model via read_file through a CompositeBackend that routes /skills/ to a virtual_mode FilesystemBackend while everything else is virtual StateBackend; skills hold procedure while matching judgement lives in compare_fit code.

Middleware order is filesystem, sql_retry_limiter, clear_old_tool_results, then answer_audit only when settings.sql_audit_model is non-empty; the retry limiter is a before_model hook that counts failed or rejected db_query results since the latest human message and at MAX_SQL_ATTEMPTS=5 appends a fixed give-up message and jumps to end, and a test ties the prompt's number to the constant.
clear_old_tool_results clears old tool output once context passes 40,000 tokens while keeping the five most recent results.

The answer audit is an after_agent hook, on by default with a Haiku model (disabled by setting off), that checks grain, filters, false zero and numbers only when SQL ran and an answer exists; on a warning it appends a second AIMessage prefixed with a warning sign, scores answer_audit either way, and fails open on any error so it never blocks or edits the answer.

The SQL path has four layers: the catalog allowlist as data, a pure sqlglot validator that regenerates the AST so only the regenerated SQL executes, an executor running in a read-only transaction with local timeouts, caller role and prepare=True, and a renderer that emits cited rows, caveats and a sources block; errors are translated into model-facing next steps.

The validator enforces a single read-only query: it rejects write nodes anywhere in the tree, INTO, locking and WITH RECURSIVE, cross-schema references and table functions, tables outside the catalog, non-allowlisted functions, placeholders and catalog casts; it resolves columns against the catalog schema, trims heavy columns from star expansion, aliases duplicate output names, and clamps LIMIT to a hard cap of 200 plus one row to detect truncation.

The executor wraps each query in conn.transaction() because the pool is autocommit, sets READ ONLY first and then transaction-local statement, lock and idle timeouts, applies the caller's role and claims via set_caller, uses prepare=True so the server refuses multi-statement strings, and limits concurrency with a semaphore sized by db_gate_slots so the checkpointer can still write.

Citation markers on SQL rows come from Column.cites declared in the catalog (kinds org, funder, activity, score, news), planned by the validator for projected id columns, and rendered by render_rows as [kind:id] prefixes; the sources block is deduplicated, capped at 8 entries, derived from source_url columns, and its grammar is a contract with the frontend pinned by tests.

Agent SQL runs as the signed-in caller under RLS: ask_access on the /agent route sets the agent_caller context variable, and the executor calls set_caller (role and JWT claims, transaction-local) after SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY, defaulting to anon when unset, so the connection returns to the pool as the owner; the catalog and validator remain the first guard. Import keeps the owner, and tools that use the shared pool directly, like compare_fit, must check access themselves via chat_user_id. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md still describes the old owner-pool design and the unmerged branch fix/ask-sql-runs-as-caller, so it lags the code.

At boot lifespan._verify_sql_catalog raises when the catalog lists a table or column the database lacks, or when the authenticated role cannot SELECT a catalogued column or anon can read only part of a table; live tables that are in neither the catalog nor KNOWN_EXCLUDED are only logged at INFO, so a new table stays invisible to the agent until someone makes a decision; KNOWN_EXCLUDED declares sensitive tables such as checkpoints, users, threads, org_members and proposals.

test_sql_catalog.py asserts what the catalog must not contain: checkpoint and user tables, contact email and phone, embeddings; it also asserts cite kinds stay within the frontend union and that the import-time self-check fires on a dangling foreign key.

instructions.md is sent verbatim as the system prompt (failing at import if empty); its rules require answering only from tool results, citing every database fact with a marker (computed figures labelled as computed), writing SQL for data questions with schema discovery, column profiling and id projection, stopping after 5 failed attempts, reporting empty results as what this user can see because queries run as the caller under row security, and delegating all fit judgement to compare_fit with its output repeated exactly.

Tests tie the prompt to the tools: every registered TOOLS entry must be named in the prompt and every citation kind a tool can emit (org, funder, activity, score, news, graph) must appear as a marker in the prompt.

Adding an Ask tool takes four edits: a never-raising, citing function in app/agent/tools/, a line in TOOLS in build.py, a mention by exact name in instructions.md (enforced by test_prompt_names_every_registered_tool), and a label in frontend/features/ask/lib/toolLabels.ts, which is unenforced because humanizeTool falls back to a humanised name; that label map is shared with the proposal copilot's tools, and the pinned tool set in test_harness.py must also be updated.

compare_fit refuses callers who are not Sangam staff or the organisation's stewards or admins by checking matching.may_run with the request's chat_user_id, returns JSON of scored matches computed in code, and the prompt instructs the model to relay a refusal and never assemble a match from db_query.

The SQL catalog allowlists 37 tables in CATALOG, while KNOWN_EXCLUDED names 22 live tables (checkpoints, users, threads, org_members, proposals, funder_matches, import bookkeeping and others) deliberately kept out, so the boot check's undeclared-table log stays quiet about them but reports tables nobody has decided on.

The backend serves three agents registered in AGENT_NAMES: /agent (Ask), /ingest (Import) and /proposal (the proposal copilot); the proposal agent reuses the Ask package's harness install and filesystem restriction but has its own tools, and the frontend toolLabels map covers its tools.
